Zinc is perhaps the most ubiquitous and versatile of all metal cofactors. Sequencing the human genome exposed more than 900
proteins that have zinc-binding domains in their structure. Not all of these proteins function as enzymes, however. Hence, it is
wrong to say zinc is a cofactor for 900 enzymes. Some of the better characterized zinc enzymes are shown in Table 4.
